text:
Pittsburgh led for nearly 19 minutes on a goal that had a 10 percent chance of going in, then lost on a third period in which Winnipeg created 2.03 expected goals to the Penguins' 0.97. Ben Kindel's tip-in at 9:27 of the second, set up by Declan Carlile and Erik Karlsson, was the only goal of the first 44 minutes. Through two periods the chances were close to even, and the game turned only when the Jets began to dominate the quality of looks.

Then the third got strange. Alex Iafallo tied it at 4:43 off a wrist shot, and Adam Lowry put Winnipeg ahead at 7:08 with a backhand that had only a 7 percent chance. Carlile answered for Pittsburgh at 8:53, a wrist shot from the Kindel and Ville Koivunen combination, and the building had barely settled when Cole Perfetti snapped home the winner nine seconds later, assisted by Josh Morrissey. Three goals came in under five minutes, all at even strength, and none of the scorers had a higher than 28 percent chance on their shot.

The scoreboard and the analytics mostly agree: Winnipeg's 3.93 expected goals to 2.80 overall, a 51 to 49 split in who deserved to win, makes this a coin flip that landed Winnipeg's way. Pittsburgh owned the shot attempts, 65 to 58, but even-strength quality was nearly identical (2.58 to 2.47). Clay Stevenson was 0.8 goals better than expected in the Jets' net, while Sergei Murashov was a shade below par for Pittsburgh. That small edge, plus Iafallo's 1.58 expected goals while on the ice, was enough.
